To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the total charge of the fragments is not sensitive to the mass asymmetry in the reaction.
the multiplicity of IMF is not a function of the mass of the system and that the multiplicity is a function of the degree of mass asymmetry.

(i) the mass independence of the multiplicity of IMFs in central collisions of symmetric reactions, and the asymmetry dependence for central collisions of asymmetric reactions, are well reproduced, and (ii) a new trend is found, which is that for peripheral collisions of asymmetric reactions a rise in the multiplicity is observed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the understanding of the role of mass and charge transfer in heavy ion reactions.
the investigation of mass independence in the fragmentation reactions of asymmetric systems and the asymmetry in the production of intermediate mass fragments in symmetric reactions.
the study of the dependence of mass and charge distributions on the degree of mass asymmetry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mass asymmetry in the colliding system has a significant effect on the fragmentation pattern of the projectile-like fragments.
the reaction mechanism is more sensitive to the mass asymmetry than the energy.
the mass-asymmetry in the reaction has a strong influence on the fragment distribution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
for symmetric systems the total number of intermediate mass fragments (IMF) increases with increasing mass asymmetry.

the total charge distributions for the intermediate mass fragment (IMF) region is almost independent of the mass asymmetry,?, in the colliding systems, while the total charge distributions are very sensitive to the mass asymmetry in the colliding system for the light mass fragment region.
the total charge distribution for asymmetric reactions is not very sensitive to the mass asymmetry.
The main takeaway from our work is that
for the same mass of the system, the multiplicity of fragments decreases with increasing asymmetry.
the mass of the system and the mass asymmetry are the two main factors which control the fragmentation process.
the mass asymmetry in the collision plays a crucial role in determining the fragment distributions.
